catalogue.name: Standard Product Delivery
catalogue.description: Idea to shipped, watched software. The full path, with gates where money and production are involved.

spec.objective: Ship working, watched software. The panel's PRD is the build brief: it is handed straight to an engineering agent, so it must be specific enough to implement and to test against.

directive.title: What should it do?
directive.description: Who it is for and what a person can do with it, in two or three sentences. The panel argues from this text and its PRD is the build brief, so a thin brief produces a thin product.
examples: A shift-swap board where staff offer a shift they cannot work, colleagues claim it, and the manager approves the swap. Used on a phone, mid-shift.

catalogue.name: Incident Response
catalogue.description: An app's alert fired. Investigate, fix the root cause with a regression test, have someone approve the release, ship it, and prove recovery from the monitor.

spec.objective: An app BOSS deployed is failing in front of users, and its own monitor raised the alarm. Find the root cause from the evidence — the app's metrics, its logs and the release that was serving — fix exactly that with a regression test that fails on the faulty release, and restore service. A person approves the release; recovery is judged by BOSS's monitor, not by the fix's author. If the evidence does not support a root cause, say so and stop rather than guess.

catalogue.description: Builds the basics first, deploys them, then improves in steps.

spec.objective: Ship the app in visible increments: the basics live first, then improved in steps. The PRD MUST end with an increment plan, headed exactly '## Increment 1', '## Increment 2', … — at most 4 increments. Increment 1 is the core of the brief (the smallest app a person can use end to end); each later increment is a small set of the remaining requirements, in the order they add the most. Each build builds only its own increment, on the branch the earlier ones left.

examples: A lunch poll for a team: anyone proposes places, everyone votes once, the poll closes at 11:30 and shows the winner. Later: recurring polls, dietary tags and a Slack reminder.

spec.objective: Investigate the named alert. Open its case, collect the evidence through the case-management, KYC and transactions connectors, map the parties related to the customer from the Knowledge Graph citing the edges, and find the closest prior determinations on that network. The AML Analyst recommends closing it as a false positive or escalating it, with a confidence, citing the evidence and any precedent it relied on. A person makes the determination and says why; agents never close an alert and never file a report. An escalation gets a drafted SAR narrative that a person reviews and files. The determination is recorded as precedent for the next related alert.

spec.objective: Investigate one Eagle exception group on NorthPeak Bank's data platform. Monitoring opens or attaches one incident for an Error group and never diagnoses. Context Enrichment and Historical Pattern are fixed graph reads, never a model. The RCA Agent proposes candidate causes citing the evidence, or says the evidence is insufficient, which runs Enrichment and Historical Pattern again (at most twice). Each candidate family goes to its lane; a confirmed false positive becomes a rule proposal. The Remediation Advisor prepares the fix; a person approves it and a different person carries it out — no agent executes. Closure re-runs the check, closes the incident and writes the precedent the next investigation finds.
